details: Renewed geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East, specifically escalating tensions between the United States and Iran, has caused crude oil prices (WTI) to surge above $100 per barrel. This rise in energy costs intensifies inflation fears, likely prompting central banks towards more restrictive monetary policies, which generally dampens investor confidence in risk assets like Bitcoin. Bitcoin has experienced four consecutive bearish sessions, declining nearly 4%, and institutional spot Bitcoin Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) are recording net outflows, suggesting weakening short-term demand. Crypto markets have moved into a broad risk-off phase, with Bitcoin and Ethereum declining ahead of U.S. inflation data.
title: US-Iran Tensions, Oil Surge Hit Crypto Demand as Bitcoin Fades
